messages:
Samira: FYI — Acme Inc reporting intermittent /embeddings failures + large tail latency. They see occasional "dimension mismatch" errors (~0.2% of calls) and P99 spikes to ~1.8s. Posting logs and repro below. thread_ts=3432109876
Ben: Can you paste exact request shape, model, headers, SDK version, and any batching config the customer uses?
Samira: Customer dump:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-SDK: redwood-js/1.4.2
body: { "model": "embed-large-v2", "input": ["short text...", "long text...", ...] }
observed: embedding_dim_expected=1536 embedding_dim_received=1537 (single vector occasionally)
```
They say they use the default client batching (no explicit max_batch_size) and sometimes hit bursts (many small requests with occasional giant doc).
Carlos: Suspect dynamic-batching interleaving small/huge requests -> padding/copy bug or serialization quirk producing off-by-one dimension. Also possible worker aggregation dtype/coercion bug.
Maya: Noted they had 429s yesterday for the same account; client fast-retries (older SDK) could change request framing in flight. Low probability but plausible.
Samira: Minimal repro from customer (they consented):
```
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```
They see dim mismatch ~1/500 runs.
Ben: Quick triage items:
- Confirm route config: check `max_batch_size` for their embeddings route (Console -> routes).
- Force no-batching: header `X-Redwood-Prefer: no-batch` or temporary `max_batch_size: 1`. If errors disappear, implicates batching.
Samira: Ran no-batch for 5k requests -> zero dim mismatches, tail latency stable (costs up). So dynamic batching implicated.
Carlos: Runtime triage plan:
- Enable `dyn_batch_debug=true` on the customer route for 30m to log per-batch composition.
- Inspect worker padding/copy code for mixed-size sequences; watch for integer overflow or off-by-one pad_to_multiple_of(16) edge-case.
- Reproduce locally with mixed tiny and very large inputs to exercise batching path.
Maya: Also check retry paths: ensure 429 retry codepaths don't alter JSON framing or create 1-off array concat bugs in SDK.
Samira: Short-term mitigations tried: set `max_batch_size: 8` for the route and add priority tag for small docs so they avoid coalescing with huge docs. Initial results: dim mismatches dropped to zero in 2k requests sample.
Carlos: If dyn_batch_debug traces show consistent interleaving (1-3 big docs with many small docs), consider a byte-size threshold to avoid mixing >64KB items with small ones. Also revisit padding routine `pad_to_multiple_of(16)` — previous patch introduced an edge-case when seq_len % 16 == 0.
Ben: Customer-facing steps to collect repro: provide the curl above, ask them to toggle `X-Redwood-Prefer: no-batch` and capture HTTP request-ids for failing runs plus raw request body base64. We want a minimal failing pair (tiny + huge) and the request-id headers.
Samira: Customer agreed; they'll send sample pairs + request-ids. ETA ~2 hours. Their deadline EOD today.
infra-bot: deployment 2026-03-16T04:12Z rolled kernel v2.3.1 to region-us-west-2 (no route config changes).
Maya: I'll assemble an escalation for SRE/Runtime including: repro command, request-ids, dyn_batch_debug output, route config snapshot, recent deploy notes, and recommended mitigations (max_batch_size=8, priority tags, route to dedicated pool).
Ben: Temporary option: migrate customer to a dedicated pool to isolate them from noisy coalescing if they are on a paid plan and need immediate SLA.
Carlos: Will schedule a short RCA slot to review padding and batching once dyn_batch_debug logs arrive.
Samira: I'll post collected artifacts when I have them. If dim mismatches continue even with `no-batch`, we'll escalate immediately. Customer is high priority, prioritizing this for EOD.
